steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **uniq -c | sort -rn** in *Text pipelines*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Which grep shows only the **uncommented, non-blank** lines of a config file?
steps.explain: `-v` inverts a pattern matching comment lines (`^#`) or empty lines (`^$`). Option 3 would also drop lines with a `#` in the middle, like `url=http://x/#a`.

steps.title: Rebuild uniq -c | sort -rn cold
prompt: Write `List<string> UniqCountSorted(List<string> lines)` that does what `uniq -c | sort -rn` does to **already-given** lines:
1. like `uniq -c`, merge only **adjacent** equal lines into `(count, line)` runs,
2. order the runs by count, highest first; runs with equal counts keep their original order,
